text: Most families in Pakistan build a house only once. The plan goes back and forth for weeks, and nobody checks the bylaws until the authority sends it back.
Naqsha is an agentic home design studio, and every agent in it runs on NVIDIA Nemotron, served by Nebius Token Factory.
You start with one message about your plot and your family. A setup agent on Nemotron 3 Super turns it into the brief in seconds.
This plot is in Islamabad, so the agent looked up the CDA's building rules with Tavily, and Nemotron 3 Ultra turned them into a rule pack, every number linked to its source.
Already have a plan from your architect? Upload a photo of it. Nemotron's vision model reads every room, and the design keeps your layout.
Four exterior concepts come back in under a minute. Pick one, and Nemotron 3 Ultra starts work as the architect.

It drafts three floor plans at once. A rules engine checks each one against the bylaws, and a fixer agent repairs the best plan with tool calls, testing every edit before it keeps it. {lda_pass} of {lda_total} bylaw checks pass.
Then Ultra writes the house in 3D as code, section by section, from a checklist of every feature in the concept. Your browser builds it as it arrives.
The vision model compares the model with the concept and sends back what's missing. Here, the match went from {match_before} to {match_after} percent.
Photos come straight from the 3D model: from the road, the street corner, the garden and the air. Every angle shows the same house.
And you can walk through it, room by room, before the first brick.
Ultra plans, fixes and writes the code. Super runs the conversation. The vision model reads drawings and checks the build. All of it on Nebius Token Factory.
Families see their home before they build it, and architects bring a checked design to the first meeting. Naqsha. Open source, built on Nemotron.
